current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 94 of them on 30 September 2026: 34 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; the Half-Life demo does not load a connectome at all by default, and DesktopFly mostly switches coded animations. No fly has been "uploaded". The newest viral claim, the FlyLeno browser talk show, is graded B (borderline C): the whole FlyWire brain really runs, untrained, but walking rhythm, homing and the choice of actions are engineered and there is no control. The Pokémon-on-a-Raspberry-Pi stream and the Rainbow Six Siege claim still publish no code (grade U). Does the real fly wiring help? Sometimes: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 23 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir and ML tasks it tied or lost (7). Even where it helps, a brainless baseline often matches the fly: in Doom the fly survives 53.3 s, shuffled wiring 6.8 s and a brainless autopilot 51.9 s, and across 13 studies with a no-brain baseline the fly network beats it in only 2. Only 9 of these 31 studies are methodologically strong, the numbers are the authors' own and none is replicated. A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs (Linux, 28 minutes) sugar input drove the feeding motor neuron to 85.2 Hz, and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 94 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 34 you can try online, 49 demo and lab videos with evidence grades, verdicts on 17 viral claims, and 31 control studies showing where the real wiring helps and where it does not.

summary: 94 entries checked on 30 Sep 2026 (12 new in the fourth check): 20 grade A, 17 B, 22 C, 4 D, 7 U and 24 datasets or tools (not graded).

Does fly wiring help? Sometimes: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 23 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir and ML tasks it tied or lost (7). Of 31 control studies, 23 have a wiring null: helps 10, no difference 5, worse 2, mixed 5, not yet scored 1. New page and data file (controls.json), 30 Sep 2026.

Where the wiring helps, a brain-free baseline often matches the fly anyway: the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 13 studies. In Doom (doom-fly-control), the fly survives 53.3 s, shuffled wiring 6.8 s, a brainless autopilot matched to the fly's average commands 51.9 s, and the best of 12 autopilot settings 53.44 s against DOOMFLY's 53.34 s.

The choice of null changes answers: in flyconnectome-nulls standard nulls beat the connectome (1.78 and 1.77 vs 1.57) but nulls that keep the sensory-motor boundary tie it (1.58 and 1.62). A fair control keeps degrees and signs, tunes the null like the real wiring, uses 3 or more shuffles with a spread, and includes a no-brain baseline.

FlyLeno ("Tonight's host: Grey Leno, piloted by Drosophila melanogaster"; Vinesauce stream, 36,763 views on 30 Sep 2026): grade B, borderline C. The whole FlyWire v783 brain runs live and untrained in the browser and its reflexes move the host, but inputs and outputs are hand-mapped, gait, homing and the choice of actions are engineered, and there is no control.
Pokémon on a Raspberry Pi 5 (Twitch, XDA Developers) and the Rainbow Six Siege fly brain (dev.ua): both still grade U after a re-check on 30 Sep 2026; no code, recording or follow-up has appeared.

New grade A entries: fly-cartpole, a careful negative result (fly mushroom bodies learn CartPole, but shuffled wiring learns about as well, 234 vs 218 steps, p = 0.20), and flybrain-connectome-benchmark, a pre-registered test of the Shiu et al. model against fly experiments (knockout sensitivity 0.77, specificity 0.99; preprint).
34 entries have a no-install link (one is a live stream); all answered our HTTP check on 30 Sep 2026, but none was played by us.

In viral demos a real connectome usually runs, but people chose the input and output neurons; DesktopFly, FlyCraft, Bad Apple, FlyDrones, the FlyBridge Minecraft farming demo and the Roblox maze race get much of their visible behaviour from scripts, stimulus, training or a synthetic network, and the Half-Life demo (grade D) builds a synthetic network by default although its videos claim MaleCNS v1.0 and "no scripted game AI".
Beat Saber, NeuroCraft, Eon's embodied fly, the Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim have no inspectable code (grade U).

Video gallery (30 Sep 2026): 49 videos, 43 of them original uploads by the project's author, lab or institution, plus one streamer's playthrough (FlyLeno) listed because the project has no video of its own; 31 of 94 catalogue entries have at least one video.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.

Build your own, tested 28 Sep 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs and no GPU: the Shiu et al. model on FlyWire v783 gave MN9 85.2 ± 3.2 Hz with sugar input at 150 Hz, 0 Hz without input, and 0 Hz in 6 of 6 trials with shuffled wiring; 6 of 6 tests passed. Pins re-checked against PyPI on 30 Sep 2026 (unchanged; full re-test due by 12 Oct 2026). Adding a FlyGym body needs Python 3.12 to 3.14 (FlyGym 2.1.0); brain-body coupling is untested by us.
uncertainty: No demo was played in a real browser; "page responds" is an HTTP check only. No project was built or run in the 30 Sep 2026 check.

Controls ledger: every number except our own Build your own run is the authors'. We recomputed 15 studies from their committed files and spot-checked 8 a second time, but re-ran none; none is replicated, and only 2 of 31 are peer-reviewed. Only 9 of 31 studies reach "strong" method quality; 16 are weak.

Ledger labels (wiring effect, fairness, quality) come from fixed yes/no rules applied to code and files; they are consistent but coarse. One label (Fly.exe, mixed) was set by hand. Retention puts very different measurements on one scale and shows direction and size, not significance. The flyvis ablation values sit in a figure and were not extracted.

The "helps" results are mostly one kind of test (does a reflex pathway still carry signal after rewiring?), which is a low bar; boundary-preserving nulls, which erased an effect in one study, have not been applied to the reflex studies.

Borderline grades: FlyLeno (B, borderline C); Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving, the null-model study and fly-brain-zero-shot are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

Several C grades and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; dev.ua blocks our fetches, and X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login. "Not the stream's code" rests on mismatches, not proof.
Stars, creation and last-push dates of 59 records were reused from our 27, 28 or 29 Sep 2026 checks and are labelled with those dates.

Not yet triaged: 29 low-star GitHub leads deferred without opening (two copy FlyGym's name and are not linked), a project with its own controls section left for the next check, 10 new Fly Brain Hub leads, about 211 repositories listed only in directories, and a popular "fly plays Gorilla Tag" video (415,612 views) that links no code. Our date-sorted video search misses older fast-growing videos.
Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated.

The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us. The FlyGym download size (about 170 MB) is an estimate from package metadata.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.

Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots from 28 Sep 2026 (29 or 30 Sep for the newest videos).

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only; Safari, Firefox and mobile untested). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
freshness_note: Catalogue re-checked 30 Sep 2026 (94 entries, 12 new); video gallery re-checked 30 Sep 2026 (49 videos); controls ledger first published 30 Sep 2026 (31 studies).
